name: J Dilla
signature: Human-feeling drum placement, warped samples, and grooves that refuse to sit perfectly on the grid.
approach: Treat the sample and the drums as one moving instrument.

name: DJ Premier
signature: Hard drums, chopped loops, scratches, and concise arrangements that put the MC first.
notable: Gang Starr, Jeru the Damaja, Nas
approach: Find one strong musical idea and make every bar land.

name: Pete Rock
signature: Layered soul textures, bright horns, thick kicks, and a deep sense of melody.
notable: C.L. Smooth, Heavy D, Brand Nubian
approach: Build the loop like a small arrangement rather than a single sample.

name: 9th Wonder
signature: Soul samples, strong drum loops, warm bass movement, and a deliberately classic feel.
approach: Keep the sample emotional, then let the drums create the head-nod.

name: Hi-Tek
signature: Soulful melodies, restrained drums, and a spacious sound that gives lyricists room.
notable: Black Star, Reflection Eternal, Talib Kweli
approach: Use texture and negative space as part of the arrangement.

name: Alchemist
signature: Dusty loops, cinematic fragments, gritty drums, and minimal arrangements.
approach: Choose a strange or striking sample and protect its mood.

name: Q-Tip
signature: Jazz-informed sampling, bass-forward grooves, unusual song structures, and subtle musical details.
notable: A Tribe Called Quest, his solo work
approach: Make the loop musical enough to feel complete before the MC enters.

name: Easy Mo Bee
signature: Dark loops, heavyweight drums, and straightforward arrangements built to support aggressive verses.
approach: Keep the beat simple, then make the drum pattern hit hard.
